record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: For equivariant map algebras M(X,a)^Γ, determine classification criteria and invariants for the isomorphism problem by extending known results for loop algebras and certain two-variable multiloop algebras to the full multiloop setting and then to more general equivariant map algebras.

evidence.quote: 4.2.1. Isomorphism problem. Characterizing EMAs up to isomorphism is one of the fundamental problems in the theory of EMAs.
It is therefore natural, though likely difficult, to try to generalize the results of both papers [ABP] and [GP07] to the multiloop case and beyond that to more general EMAs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let X be a scheme of finite type over k (or, more generally, a finitely generated commutative associative k-algebra A with X = Spec A), let g be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over k, and let Γ be a finite group acting on X (equivalently on A) by k-scheme automorphisms and on g by Lie algebra automorphisms. The equivariant map algebra is the Lie algebra

   M(X, g)^Γ = (g ⊗_k A)^Γ = { ∑ x_i ⊗ a_i ∈ g ⊗_k A : (γ·x_i) ⊗ (γ·a_i) is fixed by every γ ∈ Γ },

with bracket inherited from g ⊗ A. Important special cases include:
  (a) Untwisted multiloop algebras: A = k[t_1^{±1}, …, t_n^{±1}], Γ trivial.
  (b) Twisted multiloop algebras: A = k[t_1^{±1}, …, t_n^{±1}], Γ = Z/m_1 × … × Z/m_n acting by multiplication of t_i by primitive m_i-th roots of unity, with a compatible action on g.

The isomorphism problem asks: give a complete set of invariants and classification criteria characterizing when two equivariant map algebras M(X_1, g_1)^{Γ_1} and M(X_2, g_2)^{Γ_2} are isomorphic as Lie algebras.

Specifically:
 (1) Extend the known classification of (twisted and untwisted) loop algebras g ⊗ k[t^{±1}] up to isomorphism, and the classification of certain two-variable twisted multiloop algebras, to a complete isomorphism classification of arbitrary multiloop algebras (twisted and untwisted, in any number of variables n ≥ 1, for any finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra g and any finite-order automorphisms σ_1, …, σ_n of g).
 (2) Further extend such an isomorphism classification to general equivariant map algebras M(X, g)^Γ, identifying invariants (for example involving X/Γ, the stabilizer subgroups Γ_x, the induced actions on g, and associated cohomological data) that determine the isomorphism class.

Provide such a classification or determine the precise obstructions to it.
artifact.status_search_result: The isomorphism classification problem for equivariant map algebras remains open in general. Classifications are known for (twisted) loop algebras and certain two-variable multiloop cases, and partial progress has been made via Galois cohomology / multiloop forms over Laurent polynomial rings, but a complete isomorphism classification for general multiloop algebras and general EMAs has not appeared in the literature.

status_evidence.title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizing EMAs up to isomorphism is one of the fundamental problems in the theory of EMAs.
status_evidence.claim: The isomorphism problem for EMAs is identified as a fundamental open problem.

status_evidence.title: Galois cohomology and forms of algebras over Laurent polynomial rings
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions exist for two centreless Lie tori realized using multiloop algebras to be isotopic.
status_evidence.claim: Partial isomorphism/isotopy criteria are known for certain multiloop realizations.

status_evidence.title: Towards interpolating categories for equivariant map algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work continues to develop structural and representation-theoretic aspects of EMAs.
status_evidence.claim: EMAs remain an active research area with structural questions still being studied.
